title: What Happens If You Swallow Gum?
sources: Mayo Clinic, 'Is it true that gum stays in your stomach for seven years if you swallow it?' (gum base is not digested; it passes through, usually within days)
Milov et al., Pediatrics 1998, 'Chewing gum bezoars of the gastrointestinal tract' (large amounts swallowed often can cause blockages)

lines.text: What happens if you swallow your gum?
Well, it slides down your throat and lands right in your stomach,
where strong acid gets to work on it.
The sugar and flavor dissolve quickly, but the gum base is different.
It's a rubbery polymer, and your body simply can't break it down.
Does it stay there for seven years? No, that's a total myth.
Your gut just keeps pushing it along,
and within a few days, it's out of your system.
But if you swallow a lot of gum all at once,
lines.caps: But if you *swallow | a *lot of gum | all at *once

lines.text: it can clump together and actually block your gut.
So maybe, just spit it out.
